note: Attacker-controlled ZIP local header bytes are read from the input device into the parser's stack buffer.
The local header's extra-field length is derived directly from attacker-controlled bytes.
The parser limits the read size to the stack buffer length, but still treats the truncated bytes as an extra field.
Only the first handledextralen bytes are initialized; if the field is shorter than the stack buffer, the remaining bytes stay uninitialized.
The parser consumes the truncated buffer as TLV records even though the caller did not guarantee full initialization of the stack array.
The first TLV tag is read from bytes that may be uninitialized, which is the MSAN sink.
